text.p: Bonds closed firmer, buoyed by the more optimistic foreign tone, particularly after U.S. jobs data was seen reducing the risk of a U.S. rate rise near term, traders said.
"The market closed positive and should continue in the same vein," said one trader.
Volume was reduced by the continuing close of the Spanish market. Portugal had been closed on Thursday for the May Day holiday.
The escudo ended steady against the mark in apathetic trade.
Traders say that as long as the dollar holds above 1.72 marks, there is room for the escudo to gain, particularly if the share market continues to draw heavy foreign interest.
The currency closed at 100.34/37 per mark after opening at 100.35/38.
